reproduction_target: Generation and cross-platform benchmarking analysis of the LongBench reference dataset: 32 bulk RNA-seq libraries from 8 lung cancer cell lines (ONT PCR-cDNA, ONT direct RNA SQK-RNA004, PacBio Kinnex, Illumina) plus 10x Genomics single-cell and single-nucleus libraries sequenced on all three platforms, with Sequins and SIRV Set 4 spike-ins. Computational target: Dorado basecalling (rna004_130bps_sup@v5.1.0 / dna_r10.4.1_e8.2_400bps_sup@v5.0.0), NanoPlot read summaries, minimap2 v2.28 alignment to GRCh38 + GENCODE v44, AlignQC alignment statistics on 3M-read subsamples, transcript quantification with Salmon v1.10.2 (short read) and oarfish v0.6.2 (long read) with 50 bootstraps, tximport v1.34.0 gene-level aggregation, edgeR read-to-transcript-ambiguity overdispersion (Baldoni et al. approach), filterByExpr feature detection, spike-in (Sequins / SIRV / ERCC) analysis, TPM normalisation for cross-protocol quantification comparison, edgeR TMM + quasi-likelihood differential expression across LUAD / SCLC-A / SCLC-P, DTUrtle v1.0.3 (DRIMSeq) differential transcript usage, Cell Ranger v8.0.1 short-read single-cell/nucleus processing, BLAZE v2.5 barcode demultiplexing, FLAMES v2.0.1 long-read single-cell pipeline, MAD-based cell QC, pseudobulk construction, cellsnp-lite + Vireo genotype-based cell line assignment with doublet and ambient RNA calling, Clair3-Illumina / Clair3-RNA v1.0.10 variant calling with CCLE comparison via BCFtools v1.21, WhatsHap v2.8.0 phasing, and LongcallR allele-specific expression / splicing analysis. All results are delivered through a public Snakemake workflow (github.com/youyupei/LongBench_workflow) with a figure source map.
granularity_note: One step per named tool or named analysis invocation in the Methods section of the bioRxiv v2 full text (JATS XML retrieved 2026-07-27), following guide Step 1 coarse granularity. Wet-lab sample preparation, library preparation and sequencing are lumped into 5 W steps and are out of computational-reproduction scope. The public Snakemake repository landing page and README prose were read (including the top-level file listing showing conda/config/*.yaml environment specifications, singularity/ definition files, sub_workflows/*/Snakefile and rmarkdown/ reports); no workflow source was read line-by-line, which is stage-2 work.

steps.label: Wet-lab: culture of 8 lung cancer cell lines (H1975, HCC827, H2228 adherent; H211, H526, H69, H146, SHP77 suspension) in RPMI 1640 + GlutaMAX, 10% heat-inactivated FBS, 1% penicillin-streptomycin at 37 C / 5% CO2, passaged at 70-80% confluency.

Wet-lab: TRIzol RNA extraction from 1.5-2 M cells per line (20-80 ug, RIN 10; Nanodrop / Qubit / TapeStation QC) with Sequins mix A (SCLC-P, LUAD) or mix B (SCLC-A) and SIRV Set 4 (Iso Mix E0, ERCC, Long SIRVs) spike-ins added at ~1% of sequenced reads assuming 2% mRNA content; 10x Sequins input for ONT direct-RNA secondary flow cells.

Wet-lab: single-cell and single-nucleus preparation - FACS sorting of the 5 suspension lines on BD Aria III with 7-AAD live/dead staining (270,000 cells per line), TrypLE detachment and Countess 3 counting of the 3 adherent lines, 10x Chromium NEXT GEM single-cell 3' v3.1 capture targeting 5,000 cells, and a custom Nuclei EZ Prep-based nuclei isolation protocol (stated centrifugation speeds, buffers, RNaseOUT concentrations, FlowMi 40 um filtration) with a second 10x capture targeting 5,000 nuclei.

Wet-lab: bulk library preparation and sequencing - Illumina TruSeq v2 Stranded polyA (SuperScript III substitution, 50 C RT) on one NextSeq2000 Mid-Output flow cell; ONT direct RNA SQK-RNA004 (2 ug input, no RNA CS, NEB Induro RT) over 16 PromethION FLO-PRO004RA flow cells with a custom SQK-WSH004-based wash and reload; ONT PCR-cDNA SQK-PCB114.24 (90 min RT at 42 C, 14 PCR cycles, 4 min extension) on 3 PromethION FLO-PRO114M flow cells; PacBio Iso-Seq express 2.0 + Kinnex PCR 8-fold at AGRF on 8 Revio (non-SPRQ) flow cells.

Wet-lab: single-cell and single-nucleus library preparation and sequencing - 10x cDNA (11 PCR cycles SC, 12 cycles SN) split to Illumina (10x Library Construction Kit PN-1000190, NextSeq2000 High-Output 1.8B 100PE), ONT (single-cell protocol v9198_v114_revE_06Dec2023 with artifact removal, 10 ng cDNA input, 125 ng post-pulldown to SQK-LSK114 ligation, 0.5X bead ratio final wash, 50 ng loaded per FLO-PRO114M flow cell) and PacBio (Kinnex single-cell 12-plex concatenation kit, 2 Revio flow cells each for SC and SN).

ONT basecalling with Dorado using rna004_130bps_sup@v5.1.0 (direct RNA) and dna_r10.4.1_e8.2_400bps_sup@v5.0.0 (cDNA); reads with mean quality score < 10 discarded. Basecalling models are pinned exactly but no Dorado software version is stated, and no POD5/raw-signal accession is named anywhere - GSE303762 and the LongBench.io portal are described only as 'sequencing data', so the input to this step is not demonstrably retrievable.

Read length and quality distribution summaries with NanoPlot (Fig. 1F). No version in prose; a conda/config/NanoPlot.yaml environment specification exists in the workflow repository but was not read at stage 1 and is not a lock. No parameters stated.

Alignment of all datasets to the GRCh38 reference genome and the GENCODE v44 transcriptome with minimap2 v2.28. Version and reference/annotation releases are pinned in prose; the platform-specific presets (splice / splice:hq / map-hifi / -uf for direct RNA) and the exact GRCh38 FASTA provenance are not stated in prose.

Subsampling of genome-alignment BAMs to 3 million reads per sample and computation of alignment rate, alignment-based error and genomic feature distribution with AlignQC (Fig. 2A). No AlignQC version in prose; the workflow repository README references the container docker://vacation/alignqc by tagless name with no digest. Subsampling seed not stated.

Short-read transcript-level quantification with Salmon v1.10.2 against the GENCODE v44 transcriptome supplemented with spike-in transcripts (bulk only), using Salmon's built-in alignment and 50 bootstrap samples per run. Library type, index k-mer, bias-correction and GC-correction flags are not stated in prose.

Long-read transcript-level quantification with oarfish v0.6.2 on minimap2 v2.28 transcriptome alignments, GENCODE v44 plus spike-in transcripts for bulk, 50 bootstrap samples per run. Filter and model flags (--filter-group, coverage model, threads) are not stated in prose.
Gene-level quantification by aggregating transcript-level estimates with tximport v1.34.0. Version pinned; the countsFromAbundance / tx2gene construction options are not stated in prose.

Read-to-transcript ambiguity: estimation of extra-Poisson overdispersion parameters from 50 transcript-level bootstrap counts per run following Baldoni et al., as implemented in the edgeR package. No edgeR version, no R version and no seed for bootstrap generation are stated in prose.

Gene and transcript detection with edgeR filterByExpr, retaining features whose CPM exceeds a threshold derived from a minimum count (10 for genes, 5 for transcripts) and the median library size, in at least two of the eight cell lines. Thresholds are fully stated; no edgeR / R version is given.

Spike-in analysis: joint quantification of Sequins, SIRV Set 4 and ERCC transcripts with human transcripts in bulk datasets, with ERCC analysed separately from SIRVs because of differing capture efficiency; 'SIRV' thereafter denotes SIRV Mix 0 plus long SIRV transcripts at equal molar concentration. The spike-in annotation/FASTA source and its version are not named in prose.

Filtering and TPM normalisation for cross-protocol quantification comparison: restriction to features detected by all platforms, TPM computation with effective-length adjustment for short-read data, performed separately for human transcripts, Sequins, ERCC and SIRVs. The formula is given explicitly in Methods; the code is custom R in the public repository with no version or release tag.

Differential expression: TMM normalisation of gene and transcript counts, transcript counts further scaled by the read-to-transcript-ambiguity overdispersion following Baldoni et al., then edgeR quasi-likelihood gene- and transcript-level testing between LUAD, SCLC-A and SCLC-P on features detected across all platforms. Design matrix, dispersion-estimation settings, FDR method and significance threshold are not stated in prose; no edgeR / R version.

Differential transcript usage with DTUrtle v1.0.3 over the DRIMSeq framework: tximport v1.34.0 transcript counts restricted to detected features, DTUrtle sparse_filter with all min_* parameters = 0 to drop single-transcript genes, feature lists intersected across Illumina / ONT cDNA / ONT dRNA / PacBio, and posthoc_and_stager(ofdr=0.05, posthoc=0.1) applied to the fitted DRIMSeq models for each pairwise Sequins and human comparison.

Short-read single-cell and single-nucleus processing with Cell Ranger v8.0.1 using GENCODE v44 comprehensive annotation and the GRCh38 primary assembly. Version and annotation release pinned; expected-cells, include-introns (critical for single-nucleus) and chemistry flags are not stated in prose.
Long-read single-cell / single-nucleus barcode demultiplexing with BLAZE v2.5. Version pinned; the expected-cell-number, barcode whitelist version and threshold parameters are not stated in prose.

Long-read single-cell / single-nucleus processing with the FLAMES v2.0.1 single-cell pipeline on BLAZE-demultiplexed FASTQ to obtain gene-level quantification. Prose pins v2.0.1 while the repository README states a requirement of FLAMES >= 2.3.4 - a stated inconsistency between paper and code. FLAMES configuration JSON parameters are not given in prose.

Single-cell / single-nucleus quality filtering: median absolute deviation threshold of 3 on log-transformed nFeature and nCount, plus exclusion of cells with mitochondrial gene percentage above 3 MADs of the median; cells failing any criterion removed. Thresholds fully stated; the implementing package (scuttle / Seurat / custom) and its version are not named in prose.

Pseudobulk construction: retention of cells and nuclei detected in common across Illumina, PacBio and ONT, pooling of cell-line-assigned barcodes into per-cell-line pseudobulk FASTQ files, then processing through the identical bulk pipeline for gene- and transcript-level quantification and differential expression (spike-ins excluded from pseudo-bulk quantification). Custom code in the public repository; no version, no downsampling or depth-matching parameters stated in prose.

Genotyping at common 1000 Genomes Project human SNPs with cellsnp-lite, run first on the Illumina bulk RNA-seq data to establish the eight cell-line genotypes and then separately per single-cell / single-nucleus dataset to genotype each barcode. No cellsnp-lite version and no cellsnp-lite parameters (mode, --minMAF, --minCOUNT) are stated in prose; the 1000 Genomes common-SNP VCF release used as the reference panel is not pinned.

Cell line assignment with Vireo from the bulk and single-cell VCFs, doublets reported by default and ambient RNA estimation enabled via --callAmbientRNAs; annotations derived independently from Illumina, ONT and PacBio and merged by majority vote, ties discarded, unannotated calls ignored. Merge rule fully stated; no Vireo version and no seed for its variational inference.

Variant calling with the Clair3 series v1.0.10: Clair3-Illumina with preset ilmn for short-read RNA-seq and Clair3-RNA for bulk long-read datasets with presets hifi_mas_minimap2, ont_r10_dorado_cdna and ont_dorado_drna004; calls with QUAL < 10 discarded. Version, presets and the quality cut-off are all stated in prose; the repository deploys clair3-rna via a Singularity container whose image identity was not resolved at stage 1.

Comparison of called variants against per-cell-line somatic mutation data from the Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia (CCLE) using BCFtools v1.21. BCFtools version pinned; the CCLE release / DepMap portal version, download date and accession are not stated, and the bcftools isec/query invocation is not given in prose - an external resource consumed without a pinned snapshot.
Phasing of heterozygous variants with WhatsHap v2.8.0. Version pinned; the phasing invocation (indels, per-chromosome handling, reference) is not stated in prose.

Allele-specific expression (ASE) and allele-specific splicing (ASS) event identification with the LongcallR pipeline for long-read RNA-seq. No LongcallR version, no parameters and no significance thresholds are stated in prose.

headline.static_readiness: 0/24 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI on 11 of 24 computational steps (C3 minimap2 v2.28, C5 Salmon v1.10.2, C6 oarfish v0.6.2, C7 tximport v1.34.0, C13 DTUrtle v1.0.3, C14 Cell Ranger v8.0.1, C15 BLAZE v2.5, C16 FLAMES v2.0.1, C21 Clair3 v1.0.10, C22 BCFtools v1.21, C23 WhatsHap v2.8.0) and NI on the remaining 13. This is an unusually strong stage-1 profile on the data and code axes: the sequencing data are public and released (GEO GSE303762, public since 2025-09-01, plus an AWS Open Data mirror routed through github.com/mritchielab/LongBench.io) and the analysis code is a live public Snakemake workflow (github.com/youyupei/LongBench_workflow, last pushed 2026-06-12) whose README carries a figure-to-rule source map, so data = 2 and code = 2 on every computational step except C1, whose POD5 raw-signal input has no stated accession. The binding constraint is therefore the version axis alone. Eleven tools carry exact prose pins, which caps them at version = 1 under the Delta-2 rule because no environment closure is declared; the other thirteen steps name a tool or an analysis with no version at all (Dorado, NanoPlot, AlignQC, edgeR, cellsnp-lite, Vireo, LongcallR, and the custom TPM / MAD-filtering / pseudobulk code), which is version = 0 and drops them to NI. The repository ships conda/config/*.yaml environment specifications and singularity/ definition files but no conda-lock, no renv.lock, no image digest, no release tag and no licence, and the README itself warns that its HPC 'module load' commands are 'not portable', so environment closure cannot be claimed even in principle from what is declared. Two internal inconsistencies would also have to be resolved before execution: the paper pins FLAMES v2.0.1 while the repository requires FLAMES >= 2.3.4, and the CCLE somatic-mutation resource consumed at C22 is fetched with no pinned release.
headline.coverage: 24 computational analysis steps assessed from the bioRxiv v2 full-text METHODS subsections ('Data pre-processing and quality control', 'Gene and transcript quantification', 'Read-to-transcript ambiguity', 'Gene and transcript detection', 'Analysis of spike-in transcripts', 'Filtering and normalisation for quantification comparison', 'Differential Expression Analysis', 'Different Transcript Usage Analysis', 'Single-cell and single-nucleus RNAseq data processing', 'Cell line annotation and detection of doublets and ambient RNA in single-cell and single-nucleus data', 'Variant calling and allele-specific analyses', 'Benchmarking Analysis') plus the Data Availability and Code Availability statements, and the landing page / README prose of github.com/youyupei/LongBench_workflow. 5 wet-lab steps (cell culture, RNA extraction with spike-ins, single-cell/nucleus preparation, bulk library preparation and sequencing, single-cell/nucleus library preparation and sequencing) counted in W and out of computational-reproduction scope. Coverage = 24/29 (83%) of enumerated steps. Supplementary Table 1 (spike-in assignment) and the Supplementary Figures were not retrieved at stage 1.

gaps.where: 13 of 24 computational steps (C1, C2, C4, C8, C9, C10, C11, C12, C17, C18, C19, C20, C24)
gaps.missing: No version pin is given for Dorado itself (only the basecalling models rna004_130bps_sup@v5.1.0 and dna_r10.4.1_e8.2_400bps_sup@v5.0.0 are pinned), NanoPlot, AlignQC, edgeR, R itself, the MAD-filtering package, cellsnp-lite, Vireo or LongcallR. Eleven tools are pinned exactly in prose (minimap2 v2.28, Salmon v1.10.2, oarfish v0.6.2, tximport v1.34.0, DTUrtle v1.0.3, Cell Ranger v8.0.1, BLAZE v2.5, FLAMES v2.0.1, Clair3 v1.0.10, BCFtools v1.21, WhatsHap v2.8.0), which is why the capture claim is exact_pins_partial rather than floating. The custom analysis code (TPM normalisation, MAD cell filtering, pseudobulk construction, all figure R Markdown) carries no version or commit identifier because the repository has no tag and no release.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a software table giving an exact version (and git commit where applicable) for every tool and every R/Bioconductor package used, including the Dorado binary version, edgeR, R and the single-cell QC package, and cut a tagged release (or Zenodo DOI) of LongBench_workflow so the custom code has a citable version.

gaps.missing: No environment lockfile is claimed anywhere. The repository provides conda environment specifications (conda/config/main.yaml, NanoPlot.yaml, oarfish.yaml, clair3.yaml, whatshap.yaml, IsoQuant.yaml, PrimeSpotter.yaml, RSeQC.yaml, fastp.yaml) and Singularity definition files, plus one container referenced by bare name (docker://vacation/alignqc), but no conda-lock / pixi lock, no renv.lock, no requirements.txt with hashes, and no image digest. The README additionally states that the workflow activates the WEHI HPC software stack with 'module load' commands that the authors themselves describe as not portable and expected to fail elsewhere, so a large part of the actual environment is site-local and unserialised. The paper text mentions no container, conda specification or lockfile at all - all environment material is repository-side.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a conda-lock (or pixi.lock) resolved for at least linux-64 covering every rule's environment, replace docker://vacation/alignqc with a digest-pinned image, ship the Singularity images by digest or Zenodo DOI, and remove or make optional the site-specific module load commands so the workflow can be entered on a generic Linux host.

gaps.missing: Only 'Sequencing data are available from Gene Expression Omnibus under accession number GSE303762' and 'The LongBench data are available at https://github.com/mritchielab/LongBench.io' are stated. Neither statement names a POD5 / FAST5 raw-signal deposition, and GEO does not conventionally host raw ONT signal. The basecalling step (Dorado with pinned sup models) therefore cannot be entered from any stated accession, and every downstream long-read result inherits basecalls that can only be taken as given rather than regenerated.
gaps.how_to_close: State explicitly whether POD5 raw signal is deposited (and where - SRA, ENA or the AWS Open Data bucket), give the bucket path or accession for the signal files, and record their checksums.

gaps.where: Repository-versus-paper consistency, binding on C16 (FLAMES) and on every step whose parameters live only in the workflow
gaps.missing: The paper's Methods pin FLAMES v2.0.1 while the workflow repository README states a FLAMES requirement of >= 2.3.4 - the two declared versions are mutually exclusive, and prose alone cannot say which produced the published single-cell results. More generally, for 13 of the 24 steps the prose gives no command line at all (minimap2 presets, Salmon library type and index parameters, oarfish filter and model flags, Cell Ranger include-introns for the single-nucleus arm, FLAMES configuration JSON, cellsnp-lite mode and minMAF, Vireo seed, bcftools invocation, LongcallR thresholds), so all of these are recoverable only by reading the Snakemake rules - which is exactly the stage-2 work this assessment does not perform. There is also no LICENSE file in the repository, so redistribution rights for the analysis code are undeclared.
gaps.how_to_close: Reconcile the FLAMES version between paper and repository, lift the per-rule command lines (or at minimum the non-default flags) into a Methods supplementary table, and add an OSI-approved LICENSE to LongBench_workflow.

gaps.where: External reference and annotation resources (C1, C3, C5, C6, C10, C14, C19, C22)
gaps.missing: GENCODE v44 and GRCh38 are named as builds but the GRCh38 FASTA provenance (Ensembl vs UCSC vs GDC/1000G analysis set), its checksum and the alt/decoy contig policy are not stated, which materially changes long-read alignment. The spike-in reference used to supplement the transcriptome (Sequins mixes A/B, SIRV Set 4 Iso Mix E0, ERCC, Long SIRVs) is described biologically but its annotation/FASTA source and version are not pinned. The 1000 Genomes common-SNP panel supplied to cellsnp-lite has no release identifier. The CCLE somatic mutation data used as the variant-calling ground truth at C22 has no DepMap release, download date or accession - a continuously updated external resource consumed without a snapshot.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin the exact reference FASTA (source URL, build, checksum, alt/decoy policy), deposit or cite the versioned spike-in annotation, name the 1000 Genomes common-SNP VCF release, and cite the CCLE/DepMap release identifier and download date (ideally depositing the frozen mutation table alongside the workflow).

gaps.where: Stochastic steps C4 (3M-read BAM subsampling), C5 / C6 (50 bootstrap samples per run), C8 (overdispersion estimation from bootstraps), C20 (Vireo variational inference)
gaps.missing: No random seed is reported for any stochastic operation. The AlignQC input is a 3-million-read subsample of each BAM with no stated seed or subsampling tool; Salmon and oarfish each generate 50 bootstrap replicates whose seeds are unreported, and those bootstraps feed directly into the read-to-transcript-ambiguity overdispersion estimates that scale every transcript-level differential expression result; Vireo's assignment is a stochastic variational fit with no seed. The reported cross-platform quantification and DE comparisons are therefore not bit-reproducible.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the seed for every stochastic invocation (subsampling, Salmon and oarfish bootstraps, Vireo) and set them explicitly in the Snakemake rules so a re-run reproduces the published numbers exactly.

gaps.where: All stated code and data artifacts
gaps.missing: Every stated artifact is live but none carries a persistent identifier. github.com/youyupei/LongBench_workflow (HTTP 200, last pushed 2026-06-12) has zero releases, zero tags and no licence, so the code state that produced the paper cannot be recovered; github.com/mritchielab/LongBench.io (HTTP 200) is a mutable GitHub Pages data portal rather than an archived deposition; the AWS Open Data mirror is acknowledged in prose but no bucket name or path is given. Only GEO GSE303762 is a persistent accession, and it does not cover the code or the portal-hosted derived files.
gaps.how_to_close: Cut a tagged release of LongBench_workflow and archive it in Zenodo (or Software Heritage) with a DOI cited in the Code Availability statement, and give the AWS Open Data bucket name and prefix explicitly rather than only acknowledging the sponsorship.

gaps.where: Intermediate derived tables underpinning every comparison (C9, C11, C17, C18, C20)
gaps.missing: No machine-readable release is stated for the derived matrices on which all cross-platform claims rest: the per-platform gene and transcript count matrices, the detected-feature sets and the all-platform intersection used for quantification and DE comparison, the per-barcode cell-line assignments and merged majority-vote annotation, the QC pass/fail cell manifest, and the pseudobulk sample manifest. github.com/mritchielab/LongBench.io is described only as 'the LongBench data' with no inventory in the paper, so it cannot be established from prose whether these intermediates are published there.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish an explicit inventory of the derived artifacts (count matrices, detected-feature lists, cell-line assignment tables, QC manifests, pseudobulk manifests) with checksums, and cite that inventory from the Data Availability statement rather than pointing at a portal root.

gaps.missing: The paper's central methodological claim is that 'we standardised the computational workflow as much as possible' so that observed differences arise from the data rather than from analysis variability. The prose supports this qualitatively (Salmon and oarfish from the same developers, Clair3-Illumina vs Clair3-RNA, pseudobulk through the bulk pipeline) but gives no per-platform parameter table showing what was actually held constant and what necessarily differed (minimap2 presets, Cell Ranger vs BLAZE+FLAMES pipelines, basecalling model differences between dRNA and cDNA). Without that table the degree of standardisation - the load-bearing premise of every cross-platform conclusion - cannot be audited from prose.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a per-platform parameter table listing, for each analysis step, the exact settings used for Illumina / ONT cDNA / ONT dRNA / PacBio, marking which differences were unavoidable and which were choices.
